ASTRA · STARDIST · JEV · HARBOR

Real microscopy.
Six published images. 3 modes.

What changed with StarDist?

Measured counts improved. The complete review chain still returned no accepted counts. Astra + StarDist returned all six default specialist counts: 6.67% mean error. Standalone StarDist gets the same result, so orchestration did not improve its count accuracy.

Count comparison — lower is better

Vanilla (recovered/composite): 18.20%

Standalone StarDist: 6.67%

Astra + StarDist: 6.67%

The vanilla line is explicitly recovered/composite: five primary answers plus one separately retried timeout. The primary experiment below retains its original 5/6 coverage. Recovery used a 300-second timeout; no rejected answers were retried.

Full-chain first/last numerical candidates: 6/6 at 6.67% error. Full-chain final accepted answers: 0/6, six abstentions, zero execution errors. Candidate accuracy is diagnostic and does not replace final-output scoring.

Why high overall support did not approve an answer

Every column must reach 0.75. Method and target checks failed on all images. These scores are not calibrated probabilities of count accuracy.

Lowest error among modes answering all six images: Astra + StarDist (6.67%).

The complete BBBC001v1 counting benchmark, not a synthetic task set. Every prediction and failure is retained.

Percentage error compares each prediction with the mean of two published human counts, then averages the six errors. Lower is better. Human annotators disagree, so exact-match accuracy would be misleading.

Full harness: Astra + StarDist + Jev selection/review loop: abstained

The default full-image segmentation measured exactly 375 distinct positive nucleus instance IDs, including border instances. However, the targeted crop audit does not resolve whether irregular, closely adjacent fluorescent structures are merged nuclei or fragmented detections. Thus 375 remains a model-instance count rather than a sufficiently supported total cell count.

Limitations: Available evidence cannot resolve the failed segmentation-applicability and target-validity checks.; Crop predictions use the same model and cannot independently validate or justify corrections to the global count.; Converting nuclear instances to cells assumes one nucleus per cell; missed nuclei, merging and fragmentation remain unquantified.

Status: abstained. Tool calls: 6. Time: 159.7s.

What this experiment can tell us

  • Six previously inspected development images, not a held-out sample.
  • Prior pretraining exposure to public microscopy images cannot be ruled out.
  • Human counts disagree; their mean is the scoring reference.
  • One attempt per mode; stochastic baseline variation remains.
  • Full chain retains Jev selection and all five review requirements at 0.75 with bounded replanning; abstentions do not earn a full-dataset score.
  • Jev sees structured evidence summaries, not image pixels. Astra receives originals and selected overlays/crops.
  • Threshold profiles use the same model and do not constitute independent corroboration.
  • Count labels alone cannot establish mask precision/recall.
  • Standalone baseline is a deterministic default-tool control, reproduced inside the specialist container; new harness modes use independent Astra plans.
  • First and last candidate counts will be scored separately from accepted final answers; no best-of-N selection.

Same losslessly replicated grayscale PNG for all modes. StarDist normalizes intensities at percentiles 1/99.8 inside its tool; default/sensitive/conservative threshold profiles are fixed in code. Crops are traceable. No benchmark-specific segmentation tuning.

BBBC001 has no official train/test split. 'test' is a local Harbor routing label only.

Runtime excludes container setup. Recorded token usage and incomplete call counts appear inside each trial. No price estimate is inferred.
